tally-magenta.$description: Tally Magenta — Pink decorative accent for icons, marks, and small graphic details. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color; Decorative focus-ring and glow tint used to draw the eye to a highlighted feature card, applied as a soft 2–4px outer ring rather than a fill

action-blue.$description: Action Blue — Primary action buttons only — the lone chromatic fill in the system, used to mark conversion moments without competing with the magenta brand mark

ink.$description: Ink — Primary text, heading fills, and the dominant dark border color across cards, body elements, and form chrome. A warm near-black rather than pure black

paper.$description: Paper — Page canvas — the warm light-gray background that all white card surfaces sit on. The signature surface of the system

white.$description: White — Card surfaces, form previews, input fields, and icon fills on the canvas. Provides the only bright surface layer

mist.$description: Mist — Subtle elevated or muted surface for secondary panels, code blocks, and hover washes — a half-step darker than pure white

graphite.$description: Graphite — Secondary text, helper copy, and tertiary borders on icons and body elements

ash.$description: Ash — Muted borders, inactive dividers, and low-emphasis strokes for icons and form elements

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

black.$description: Black — Heading borders, the dark header CTA button fill, and the highest-contrast button text — reserved for moments that need maximum weight

purple-to-pink.$description: Purple-to-Pink — Underline and streak flourishes under display headlines — a short linear sweep from violet to magenta that replaces the traditional squiggle

inter.$description: The only typeface across the entire system. Used for display headlines at 64px weight 800, section headings at 30–36px weight 700, subheadings at 22–26px weight 600, body at 16–18px weight 400–500, and caption/label at 13–14px weight 500. The tight -0.031em tracking and high x-height make it read like a serif replacement at display sizes.
